scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Tripuri dance originated among the indigenous tribal communities living in the hills of Tripura in northeastern India, predominantly the Tripuri people who constitute over half of the tribal population, alongside the Reangs, Marmas (Mogs), and Halams.
The dances historically evolved around jhum (shifting cultivation) and seasonal agrarian rituals.
Over time, specific clan traditions developed, such as the Reang clan's Hojagiri dance and the Marma community's Sangrai and Owa dances.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Dances are tied to the agricultural calendar, seasonal shifts, and religious observances.
Goria dance accompanies prayers during April's Garia Puja for a bountiful crop.
Lebang Boomani is performed during the pre-monsoon lull; the number of lebang insects caught is believed to indicate harvest prosperity.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Folk and Tribal Dances of Tripura, Karnataka and Uttar Pradesh (https://archive.org/details/dni.ncaa.CCRT-94-UMHB)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The performance structure varies by specific tradition.
The Goria dance is performed by both men and women moving village to village in a gradually increasing tempo using mudras that mimic natural movements.

In the Reang clan's Hojagiri dance, teams of four to six young women balance props like bottles or earthen pitchers on their heads and lamps on their hands while moving only the lower half of the body.
Watch for Tokka Clapping, Lebang Scarf Catch, Prop Balancing Lower Isolation.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Processions moving across village terrain; small group floor patterns of 4 to 6 members.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Tripuri dances are accompanied by regional indigenous musical instruments.
Sowing and general folk dances like Goria use drums and flutes.
Listen for the Khamb drum, Pung, Flute, Sarinda.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 110 beats a minute.

A vibrant acoustic blend dominated by the sharp, repetitive crack of bamboo tokka clappers, deep resonant thuds of khamb and pung percussion, melismatically floating bamboo flute melodies, and high-pitched sarinda strings.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers perform in outdoor village spaces, hill slopes, places of worship, and temples.
For dances like Lebang Boomani, women adorn themselves with silver chains, rings, and bangles, along with bronze ear and nose rings, while carrying colorful scarves.
In Hojagiri, dancers balance props such as earthen pitchers, bottles, and lit or unlit lamps.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Several Tripuri dances are sacred rituals performed during religious festivals and at places of worship, such as the Goria dance during Garia Puja, the Hai-hak dance at goddess Lakshmi's place of worship, and the Marma community's Buddhist Owa dance.

visual_brief.costume_notes: Dancers perform in outdoor village spaces, hill slopes, places of worship, and temples. For dances like Lebang Boomani, women adorn themselves with silver chains, rings, and bangles, along with bronze ear and nose rings, while carrying colorful scarves. In Hojagiri, dancers balance props such as earthen pitchers, bottles, and lit or unlit lamps. Marma Buddhist dances such as Owa are performed in connection with visits to Buddhist temples and river sites where paper or toy boats are launched.
visual_brief.setting_notes: Dances are tied to the agricultural calendar, seasonal shifts, and religious observances. Goria dance accompanies prayers during April's Garia Puja for a bountiful crop. Lebang Boomani is performed during the pre-monsoon lull; the number of lebang insects caught is believed to indicate harvest prosperity. Post-harvest dances include Mamita and the Halam community's Hai-hak dance, performed to honor the goddess Lakshmi. The Marma community's Owa dance takes place on the full moon day of Ashwin in the Bengali calendar, and Sangrai occurs during the month of April (Chaitra). Mosak sulmani serves as a hunting ritual dance.
